title: Concrete finite-level realization and the data for etale normalization
statement: For schemes X,Y, g:Y→X, an adic coefficient datum d on A, an adic tower M on X and U in Y.ProEt, put B_n=AdicCompletion(I,A)/(I AdicCompletion(I,A))^(n+1) with its consecutive quotient q_n [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. Retain the original ring, quotient, scalar-forgetting arrow and LisseTowerEtaleDescent record verbatim. For an already specified family D_n of etale B_n-complexes define LisseTowerEtaleNormalization to contain only its normalization/realization fields: delta_n, coherent etale universality [def-weil-pbc-etale-universal-normalization], universality and restriction coherence for every algebraic constant arrow, the realization functors on V and W, model and actual comparisons, coefficient interchange, and the exact actual_normalized and model_normalized equations of the original record. No boundedness, local-marking or stalk condition is included in this auxiliary record. For f:Z→X define the fixed realization explicitly: restrict B_n-scalars along the canonical bijection A/I^(n+1)→B_n, convert fixed module sheaves to module presheaves, and sheafify them along constant sections of the actual pulled finite coefficient ring. The scalar map uses the inverse of the canonical constant-ring comparison and the constant inverse-image isomorphism. This construction is an additive equivalence; B_n is finite. All module and functor data are concrete, with no choice from a mere existence assertion.

proof.text: Move the original coefficient declarations and descent record without altering their signatures or bodies. Specify the normalization-only record for a fixed family of levels.

The constant-sheaf adjunction and inverse-image adjunction identify the canonical constant inverse-image map with the isomorphism between left adjoints. Pull back the proved level constant comparison and compose it with this map.

The scalar map is the sheafification unit followed by a ring-sheaf isomorphism, so it is locally injective and locally surjective. The fixed-to-ringed module-sheaf equivalence then applies. Derive this additive equivalence.

The canonical completion quotient map is bijective for a finitely generated ideal. Its target is finite by surjectivity, and restriction along its ring equivalence is an equivalence, as is the induced sheaf and derived restriction. Compose with the preceding derived realization.

    (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X)

    (M : AdicTower X d) (U : Y.ProEt)

      (Sheaf U.left.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (lisseTowerEtaleRing d n))))
